# Results — Study 439 (Linear Regression Channel)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **the slope
of a fitted regression line is a better trend signal than a moving average** — tested by turning
the 60-day OLS log-price slope into a long/flat timing rule on SPY and racing it, **net of costs
and excess-vs-excess**, against (a) buy-and-hold and (b) the equivalent price-vs-SMA rule. One
execution lag (signal at close t → return t+1). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** (auto-adjusted) closes — SPY (public, no key) |
| Window | **2005-01-03 → 2026-06-12** (As-of 2026-06-12; **21.4** years; **5,395** daily bars) |
| Fingerprint | SPY close sha1[:12] = **`aeda2bbca066`** |
| Indicator | **60-day** rolling OLS slope of log(close), annualised (closed-form, exact) |
| Rules | slope long/flat (headline), slope long/short, benchmark price-vs-60-day-SMA long/flat |
| Timing / costs | enter the **next** close (one lag); **1 bp** one-way × |Δposition| (turnover as NAV fraction); shorts pay **50 bp/yr** borrow |
| Panel (cross-check) | SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, JPM, XLE |

## The race — slope rule vs SMA rule vs buy-and-hold (NET, excess-vs-excess, long/flat)

The Signal axis is a one-sample **HAC (Newey-West) t** on the daily **active** return (strategy
net minus buy-and-hold). A REAL stamp needs t ≥ 2 on this active series — the head-to-head edge
over the market the rule is trading, not its raw return in a 21-year bull market.

| Rule | net Sharpe (excess) | Sharpe gap vs B&H | active HAC *t* | time-in-mkt | turnover/yr | net CAGR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Buy & hold** | **+0.647** | — | — | 100% | 0.0 | +11.08% |
| **Regression slope (60d)** | +0.711 | **+0.063** | **−1.51** | 72% | 3.26 | +7.81% |
| Price-vs-SMA (60d) | +0.604 | −0.043 | −2.03 | 72% | 15.92 | +6.17% |

Read it carefully. The slope rule's net Sharpe (+0.711) edges buy-and-hold (+0.647) — but that
gap is **not statistically real**: the daily active return has **HAC t = −1.51** (it is, if
anything, *negative*). On **growth** buy-and-hold wins outright (+11.08% vs +7.81%/yr) because
the rule sits in cash ~28% of the time during an up-market. The slope's higher Sharpe is pure
volatility-trimming, not alpha. The SMA rule is worse on every axis except that it, too, fails to
beat the market.

## The decisive test — block-permutation placebo

Observed mean daily active return (slope net minus buy-and-hold): **−1.641 bps/day**. A 2,000-draw
**21-day-block** permutation of the rule's own timing (preserves its persistence, destroys its
alignment with returns) gives **p = 0.676** — the observed bar sits squarely inside the luck
cloud, left of zero. A real edge would sit far in the right tail. It does not.

## Costs — there is nothing for costs to kill

| one-way cost | net Sharpe (slope) | Sharpe gap vs B&H | active *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bp | +0.713 | +0.066 | −1.50 |
| 0.5 bp | +0.712 | +0.065 | −1.51 |
| 1.0 bp | +0.711 | +0.063 | −1.51 |
| 2.0 bp | +0.708 | +0.061 | −1.53 |
| 5.0 bp | +0.699 | +0.052 | −1.56 |

The active *t* barely moves with cost — because the edge was never there. This is not a "great
signal eaten by frictions" story; it is "no signal."

## Robustness — window sweep (is the 60-day a cherry pick?)

| window | net Sharpe (slope) | Sharpe gap vs B&H | active *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 20 | +0.552 | −0.093 | −2.23 |
| 40 | +0.465 | −0.175 | −2.44 |
| **60** | **+0.711** | **+0.063** | **−1.51** |
| 100 | +0.595 | −0.053 | −1.91 |
| 200 | +0.711 | +0.058 | −1.03 |

No window from 20 to 200 days produces an active *t* that clears +2; most are negative. The
60-day is not hiding a missed edge.

**Long/short variant (SPY, 60d, net):** Sharpe **+0.205**, Sharpe gap **−0.442**, active *t*
**−1.54**. Shorting a market that mostly goes up is, predictably, a loser.

## Myth check — does the slope beat a moving average?

The whole pitch is that the regression slope improves on a moving average. Head-to-head, the
slope rule's active *t* (**−1.51**) is essentially the SMA rule's (**−2.03**) — **both fail to
beat the market**. The slope's *only* genuine difference is **lower turnover** (3.26 vs 15.92
round-trips/yr), because the slope flips sign less often than price crosses its average. That is a
smoothness property, not an edge. **"Beats a moving average" is NOT SUPPORTED.**

## Cross-instrument — the SPY "win" doesn't generalise

| ticker | net Sharpe (slope) | Sharpe (B&H) | gap | active *t* | result |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--|
| SPY | +0.711 | +0.647 | +0.063 | −1.51 | beat (not sig.) |
| QQQ | +0.560 | +0.793 | −0.233 | −3.01 | lost |
| AAPL | +0.959 | +0.963 | −0.004 | −1.82 | lost |
| MSFT | +0.543 | +0.683 | −0.140 | −2.36 | lost |
| JPM | +0.310 | +0.543 | −0.234 | −2.51 | lost |
| XLE | +0.168 | +0.404 | −0.236 | −1.96 | lost |

The slope rule beats buy-and-hold on **1 of 6** names — and that one (SPY) isn't significant.
A rule whose only positive instance is the ticker you tested first is the oldest mirage there is.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel with **planted, sign-persistent trends** (regimes a slope *can* ride),
the inference behaves exactly as it must:

| planted edge | slope net Sharpe | B&H Sharpe | Sharpe gap | active *t* | permutation *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00/yr** (no edge) | −0.028 | +0.112 | −0.140 | **−0.72** | 0.714 |
| **+0.50/yr** (strong trend) | +2.263 | +1.556 | +0.706 | **+2.44** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted trend the slope rule sits at t ≈ 0 and does not manufacture significance from
noise; a strong planted trend lights it up (t = +2.44, permutation p ≈ 0). The machinery *can*
detect a slope edge when one exists — so the real-tape **null is a true negative**, not a broken
harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The slope rule's daily out-performance over buy-and-hold has **HAC t = −1.51**
  (block-permutation **p = 0.68**) — negative and nowhere near the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar. No window
  from 20–200 days clears it, and it loses to buy-and-hold on 5 of 6 panel names.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The wafer-thin SPY net Sharpe edge (**+0.711** vs **+0.647**) is not
  significant, inverts cross-section, and the long/short variant collapses to Sharpe **+0.205**.
  There is no edge for costs to kill — even at zero cost it doesn't beat the market.
- **Beats a moving average? — NOT SUPPORTED.** Slope active *t* (**−1.51**) ≈ SMA active *t*
  (**−2.03**), both sub-zero. The regression slope's only genuine property is **lower turnover**
  (3.26 vs 15.92/yr) — a smoothness artefact, not alpha. A rolling OLS slope is a *linear* filter
  of past prices: mathematically a relative of the moving average, dressed up as a leading
  indicator. It is a fine drawing tool and a non-edge.
